headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: long-run uptrend holds, but price is resting on its key floor

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's long-run posture is still to grow acquisition, because the 3-6 month uptrend holds, but today it should be applied carefully. Bitcoin is down about 8% in a week, a Rally watch drop window opened today, and price sits just above its 200-day average ($73,123). In practice: keep acquisition running in small, easy-to-pause steps, hold trader-targeted promotions and keep a budget reserve, and lead with trust and education. Step up only after a close back above $81,141 (the 50-day average); a close under $73,123 is the cue to shift budget toward keeping existing users. This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($73,800) is only about 1% above its 200-day average ($73,123), which is still rising.
Up about 16% over 90 days; about 94% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But down about 8% in 7 days and 10% in 30 days; 21 days under the 50-day average ($81,141).
Fear & Greed at 29 (fear); hotter US inflation and Fed talk of more rate rises weigh on the near term.
watch: Bitcoin is sitting about 1% above its 200-day average, the main line holding up the long-run uptrend, just as US inflation came in hot and a Rally watch drop window opened. A close below $73,123 would put that uptrend in question, while a close back above $75,250 would ease the pressure.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the coming week looks soft and Bitcoin is now sitting right on the line that matters most. At about $73,800 it has closed under its 50-day average for 21 days, sits about 9% below it and about 12% below its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 29 (fear); US inflation came in hotter than expected yesterday (PANews), which is adding to the gloom. A normal week swings about $2,957, so a close above $75,250 (top of a typical week's swing) would ease the pressure, a close below $73,123 (the 200-day average) would turn the week clearly down, and in between it stays choppy. A Rally watch drop window opened today, so this is a week for calm, safety-first messaging rather than promotions.

The next month is mixed and leaning softer. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 16% higher and about 94% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 10%, and news is taking a little off: Fed officials Logan and Bowman said they may back more rate rises ahead of the 8 December meeting (PANews). Price must win back $81,141 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading. Hold bigger campaign pushes until that average is back in reach.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is only about 1% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 5% over 90 days, and news is adding a little: big banks including Goldman Sachs and Citi committed about $270 million to a joint stablecoin project and Miami-Dade County now takes Bitcoin for property tax (PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,123 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,706 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A close below the 200-day average is what would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
